Nested logit regression

Source: R/estimators.R
nlogit.Rd

Fits the two-level nested logit (McFadden 1978) in its utility-maximization- consistent form, the one mlogit and Stata's nlogit (RUM-consistent) use: alternatives are partitioned into nests, and each nest \(m\) has an inclusive-value parameter \(\lambda_m\) that governs the correlation of the errors within the nest (\(\lambda_m = 1\): no correlation, the multinomial logit; values in \((0, 1)\) are consistent with utility maximization for all covariate values).

Usage

nlogit(
  formula,
  data,
  nests,
  equal_lambda = FALSE,
  id = NULL,
  alt = NULL,
  ref = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  fe = NULL,
  se = c("analytic", "opg", "robust", "cluster", "bootstrap", "none"),
  cluster = NULL,
  nboot = 200L,
  cores = 1L,
  start = NULL,
  maxit = 1000L,
  reltol = 1e-10
)

Arguments

formula

A formula; see the section "Two data layouts" of mnl().

data

A data frame.

nests

A named list of character vectors assigning every alternative (response level) to exactly one nest, e.g. list(fast = c("air", "train"), slow = c("bus", "car")).

equal_lambda

If TRUE, one inclusive-value parameter is shared by all (non-singleton) nests.

id, alt

For the long layout, the names of the case and alternative columns of data. Leave both NULL for the wide layout.

ref

The base (reference) alternative: a level of the response. Default: the first level.

weights

Optional frequency weights: a column name in data or a numeric vector with one entry per row (constant within a case in the long layout).

offset

Optional offset on the utility scale: in the long layout a column name or a vector with one entry per row; in the wide layout an \(n \times J\) matrix (columns in level order).

fe

Optional column name in data identifying units that receive alternative-specific fixed effects.

se

Standard errors: "analytic" (inverse observed information, default), "opg" (inverse outer product of the scores, the BHHH form that mlogit reports for the nested logit and HEV), "robust", "cluster" (needs cluster), "bootstrap" (nonparametric over cases, or over clusters when cluster is given, with nboot refits from the full-sample estimate; the replicates are kept in object$boot and confint() can report percentile intervals), or "none". With fe, the bootstrap resamples units (a unit drawn twice counts as two units, each with its own fixed effects; a case bootstrap would give units random numbers of cases and a second incidental-parameters bias) and covers the slopes only: the alternative-specific constants and the unit dummies refer to reference units that change between replicates, so their bootstrap standard errors are NA, and first_difference() refuses intervals that need them (use analytic, robust, or cluster standard errors for those). A replicate whose fixed effects cannot be built (an alternative left unconnected to the base) counts as failed, the standard errors are then conditional on resamples in which they can be built, and the fit stops when fewer than half the replicates are usable. A cluster given with fe must nest the units (whole units are drawn; one that cuts across units is refused). The replicates are not jackknife-corrected.

cluster

Optional cluster identifier (a column name in data or a vector aligned to its rows, constant within a case); supplying it selects se = "cluster" unless se is given explicitly.

nboot

Number of bootstrap refits for se = "bootstrap" (default 200).

cores

Number of parallel workers for the bootstrap (a PSOCK cluster; default 1). set.seed() before the call makes the resamples reproducible; serial and parallel runs use different random streams.

start

Optional starting values: the full parameter vector in the order of coef() but on the INTERNAL scale, which differs from coef() for the structural parameters (the logarithms of the inclusive values, scales, and standard deviations; the free Cholesky elements with a log diagonal for the multinomial probit covariance). object$theta of an earlier fit is on that scale. Rarely needed for mnl(), whose log-likelihood is globally concave; the other estimators start from the mnl() estimates (and imnl() from a multistart grid), so start serves to probe another basin of a non-concave likelihood.

maxit, reltol

Controls for the BFGS stage passed to stats::optim() (the plain mnl() is solved by damped Newton steps first, with BFGS as the fallback); the Newton polish that follows runs up to 25 further iterations with the analytic Hessian of the logit family or central differences of the analytic gradient otherwise.

Value

An object of class c("nlogit", "choicemodel"); as mnl(), with the inclusive-value parameters named "lambda:<nest>" (or "lambda"). predict(type = "prob_conditional") gives the within-nest probabilities.

Details

With \(V_{ij}\) as in mnl() and \(I_{im} = \log\sum_{k \in B_m} e^{V_{ik}/\lambda_m}\) over the alternatives of nest \(m\) available to case \(i\), $$P(y_i = j) = \frac{e^{V_{ij}/\lambda_m}}{\sum_{k \in B_m} e^{V_{ik}/\lambda_m}} \cdot \frac{e^{\lambda_m I_{im}}}{\sum_l e^{\lambda_l I_{il}}}, \qquad j \in B_m.$$ The inclusive-value parameters are estimated on the log scale and reported on the natural scale with delta-method standard errors; the z statistics of the summary test \(\lambda = 1\) (the multinomial logit within that nest). Test IIA jointly with lr_test(mnl_fit, nlogit_fit) (the restriction \(\lambda = 1\) is interior). A singleton nest's parameter does not enter the likelihood and is fixed at 1 (with a message). Everything else – layouts, weights, offsets, fixed effects, standard errors – is as in mnl(). Starting values come from the multinomial logit fit; the fit is run from \(\lambda = 1\) and \(\lambda = 0.7\) and the better optimum kept.

References

McFadden, D. (1978). Modelling the choice of residential location. In A. Karlqvist et al. (eds.), Spatial Interaction Theory and Planning Models, 75-96. North-Holland.

Train, K.E. (2009). Discrete Choice Methods with Simulation, 2nd ed., chapter 4.

See also

mnl(), hev(), lr_test()

Other estimators: hev(), imnl(), mnl(), mnprobit(), remnl(), rologit()

Examples

set.seed(3)
d <- rnlogit(1500, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5), d = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.3)),
             nests = list(n1 = c("a", "b"), n2 = c("c", "d")), lambda = c(0.6, 0.8))
m <- nlogit(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, nests = list(n1 = c("a", "b"), n2 = c("c", "d")))
#> Inclusive-value parameter(s) above 1 (lambda:n2): outside the range consistent with random-utility maximization for all covariate values; the nesting may be wrong or unnecessary (lr_test() against the mnl() fit).
summary(m)
#> Nested logit (2 nests) 
#> Call: nlogit(formula = y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, nests = list(n1 = c("a", 
#>     "b"), n2 = c("c", "d")))
#> Alternatives: a, b, c, d  (base: a)
#> 
#> Outcome equations (alternative:term):
#>               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> b:(Intercept)   0.3304     0.1450   2.279 0.022667 *  
#> b:x1           -0.7676     0.3098  -2.478 0.013228 *  
#> b:x2            0.6039     0.2532   2.385 0.017060 *  
#> c:(Intercept)  -1.0516     0.6864  -1.532 0.125518    
#> c:x1            0.7067     0.1873   3.774 0.000161 ***
#> c:x2           -0.9434     0.3282  -2.874 0.004047 ** 
#> d:(Intercept)  -0.3608     0.3945  -0.915 0.360305    
#> d:x1            0.6553     0.2038   3.216 0.001301 ** 
#> d:x2            0.2190     0.3173   0.690 0.489955    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Inclusive-value parameters lambda (z tests are against 1 = multinomial logit; the joint test is lr_test() against the mnl() fit):
#>           Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> lambda:n1   0.4146     0.1751  -3.343 0.000829 ***
#> lambda:n2   1.3286     0.6937   0.474 0.635727    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Standard errors: analytic. Log-likelihood -1554.187 on 11 parameters, 1500 cases. AIC 3130.37, BIC 3188.82.
lr_test(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d), m)
#> Likelihood-ratio test
#>   LR = 10.5298 on 2 df, p = 0.00517
